unmapped_concepts.suggested_label: Coupled Widening and Deepening in Procedural Memory Evolution
unmapped_concepts.suggested_description: A situation concept that describes the dual-axis evolution process where external skill libraries simultaneously expand coverage through gap minting and harden reliability through failure-driven rewrites. Encompasses: coverage pool distillation, failure-based skill contrasting, iterative round progression. Excludes: single-axis optimization strategies.
unmapped_concepts.concept: The paper demonstrates that procedural memory evolves effectively along two coupled axes—widening the skill bank by minting procedures for uncovered subtasks and deepening existing skills by contrasting failures with successful executions. Ablations confirm that neither mechanism alone matches the performance of their combined application across evolution rounds.
unmapped_concepts.reason: This captures the specific dual-axis system dynamic presented in the study which combines widening and deepening.
unmapped_concepts.Accelerationist Interpretation: Accelerationists view coupled widening and deepening as an optimal scaling mechanism for agentic systems, allowing rapid expansion of operational capabilities followed by rigorous consolidation without requiring expensive model weight updates.
unmapped_concepts.Safetyist Interpretation: Safetyists interpret the coupling of widening and deepening through the lens of bounded adaptation, where failure-driven deepening and conservative replay gates act as necessary checks against runaway error accumulation and proxy reward hacking.
unmapped_concepts.Skeptic Interpretation: Skeptics view the necessity of dual-axis memory evolution as evidence of underlying model fragility, arguing that complex procedural scaffolding is merely patching inherent foundation model limitations rather than achieving genuine understanding.

unmapped_concepts.concept: To overcome a model's default procedural shortcuts, retrieval must be conditioned on user preferences and the default tool set must be actively scoped so that competing shortcuts are unavailable, ensuring the agent executes the requested technique.
